Simple wrapper for pathway enrichment methods

Source: R/jamenrich-er-methods.R
jam_enricher.Rd

Simple wrapper for pathway enrichment methods, to produce enrichment results suitable for use with multienrichment analysis.

Usage

jam_enricher(
  genedata,
  pathwaydata,
  enrich_method = c("ORA", "GSEA"),
  universe = NULL,
  genedata_params = list(ann_lib = "org.Hs.eg.db"),
  pathwaydata_params = list(ann_lib = "org.Hs.eg.db"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

genedata

list named by the Enrichment condition, where each list element contains a suitable form of data. Each 'genedata' will be tested for enrichment independently.

Expected formats:

  • character vector of genes, which represent "gene hits". Compatible with 'ORA' and cannot be used with 'GSEA'.

  • integer vector of integer signs limited to 1 or -1, named by gene. Compatible with 'ORA' and cannot be used with 'GSEA'. The sign applies directionality to genes, is used to define 'direction' in the pathway, but not used for enrichment itself.

  • numeric with scalar values, named by gene. Compatible with 'GSEA' and cannot be used with 'ORA'. The numeric value ranks the genes, and is applied to directionality of the results.

  • data.frame of gene stats, with columns: 'gene', 'pvalue', 'fold' in some conceptual form. Compatible with 'ORA' and 'GSEA'.

pathwaydata

one of the following:

  • Pathways: list of pathways, named by pathway, whose values are individual genes assigned to each pathway.

  • List of Pathway Sources: list named by pathway source, each containing a list of pathways as described above, named by pathway and containing pathway genes. Each Pathway Source will be analyzed one by one, independently.

enrich_method

character string with enrichment method to perform:

  • 'ORA': uses clusterProfiler::enricher() for a standard hypergeometric (Fisher's Exact) test of enrichment.

  • 'GSEA': uses clusterProfiler::GSEA() for ranked gene set enrichment analysis. It calls 'fgsea' for fast-GSEA.

universe

one of the following:

  • character vector of genes to define the background universe for the enrichment test. The same universe is used for all enrichment tests. When NULL as by default, it uses all genes defined in 'pathwaydata'.

  • list named by names(genedata) to define a universe for each individual entry in 'genedata'. Todo: Consider unique universe by genedata/pathwaydata.

genedata_params

list to manage 'genedata'.

  • refresh_genes: logical whether to update gene symbols using genejam::freshenGenes()

  • ann_lib: character with Bioconductor library to use when 'refresh_genes' is TRUE.

  • handle_multiple: character string in genejam::freshenGenes(), default "best_each" uses the best match for each gene symbol per row.

  • empty_rule: character how to handle empty gene 'SYMBOL'. Default 'empty' leaves the value blank. Other options are 'original' to keep the original value, or 'na' to insert NA.

  • pvalue_cutoff,fold_cutoff: numeric thresholds used when genedata is supplied as a data.frame. It will define gene statistical hits using these thresholds. Default NULL will not apply thresholds, and will not define hits.

  • gene_colnames,pvalue_colnames,fold_colnames: character vectors with patterns used to match column names when 'genedata' contains a data.frame. These columns are required. The 'gene_colname' is used as the initial gene, and will be used when refresh_genes=TRUE.

  • tstat_colnames: character (optional) pattern for t-statistic column name when 'genedata' contains a data.frame. It is only used when rank_strategy='t-statistic'.

  • rank_strategy: character string used when genedata contains a data.frame:

    • 'signed-P' (default) uses the -log10(Pvalue) multiplied by the sign of the fold change. It produces the same rank order as using the t-statistic, useful when the 't' column is not available.

    • 't-statistic' uses the t-statistical column.

    • 'P-value' uses the -log10(Pvalue) to rank entries.

    • 'log2fold' uses the fold column to rank entries. Although a common default, we recommend the signed-P for improved resolution.

  • try_list: passed to genejam::freshenGenes() to determine which annotation methods to search when resolving to gene SYMBOL. They are handled in priority order, there 'best_each' will return the first (best) result for each input gene. When input genes are entirely integer values, they are assumed to be ENTREZID values, which skips this step.

pathwaydata_params

list to manage 'pathwaydata'.

  • See 'genedata_params' for description of most fields.

  • pathway_colnames: character vector with patterns for preferred pathway column names, the first match with find_colname(pattern, x) is used as the pathway name. For the purpose of this process, only the pathway name is retained, and all other annotations should be retrieved separately as needed.

verbose

logical whether to print verbose output.

...

additional arguments are passed to internal functions.

Value

nested list of enrichResult objects.

  • list named by 'genedata', each with:

  • list named by 'pathwaydata', each with

  • list named by 'enrich_method', each with

  • 'ORA'=enrichResult or 'GSEA'=gseaResult

In addition, an attribute 'pathwaydata' is added with the updated pathwaydata after process_pathwaydata()

Details

Workflow

  1. Iterate each 'genedata'

    • Validate data format.

    • Optional: Update gene annotations using genejam::freshenGenes().

    • Produce data.frame with numeric hit and sign.

  2. Iterate each 'pathwaydata'

    • Optional: Update gene annotations using genejam::freshenGenes().

    • Produce data.frame TERM2GENE suitable for 'clusterProfiler'.

Note that gene annotations can be synchronized to ensure the 'genedata' and 'pathwaydata' both use the same version of annotation.

  1. Iterate each 'enrich_method'

    • ORA - over-representation analysis, aka hypergeometric enrichment, Fisher's Exact Test.

    • GSEA - gene set enrichment analysis, using fast-GSEA (fgsea)

  2. Collate results

    • Convert to enrichResult or gseaResult.

    • Return all results as a nested list, indexed by:

      • 'genedata'

      • 'pathwaydata'

      • 'enrich_method'
